textbookText: ii) How is it that the gametes formed by hybrid parents can also be pure? Ans:- Gametes formed by hybrid parents are pure because of law of segregation each gamete receives only one allele from each gene pair. 9. Explain the role of mitosis and meiosis in the reproduction of organisms. Ans:- Mitosis and meiosis both play vital roles in the reproduction and continuity of life in organisms. Mitosis is a type of cell division that occurs in somatic (body) cells and is responsible for growth, development, and repair. During mitosis, one parent cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each containing the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. This process ensures that genetic information remains constant, helping in asexual reproduction, where offspring are genetically identical to the parent. On the other hand, meiosis occurs in reproductive cells (gametes such as sperm and egg) and is essential for sexual reproduction. It reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes (haploid). When male and female gametes fuse during fertilization, the normal diploid number of chromosomes is restored. Thus, meiosis introduces genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment, while mitosis maintains genetic stability. Together, these two processes ensure both the continuity and diversity of life. 10. What will happened if meiotic cell division does not occur in the reproductive ceil of an organism? Explain. Ans:- If meiotic cell division does not occur in the reproductive cells of an organism, gametes (sperm and egg cells) will not be formed with half the number of chromosomes. Instead, the reproductive cells would contain the full or diploid number of chromosomes. As a result, when fertilization takes place, the zygote formed would have double the normal number of chromosomes, leading to serious abnormalities or the death of the embryo. In some cases, fertilization may not occur at all because proper gametes are not produced. Therefore, meiosis is essential for maintaining the normal chromosome number from generation to generation and for ensuring genetic variation among offspring. Without meiosis, sexual reproduction and the continuation of species would not be possible.
11. Explain with an example that Mendel's experiment can be done not only in plants but also in animals.
Ans:- Mendel’s experiment can be done not only in plants but also in animals because the basic principles of inheritance
dominant and recessive traits apply to all living organisms. For example, in guinea pigs, the gene for black fur is dominant
(B) and the gene for white fur is recessive (b). When a pure black guinea pig (BB) is crossed with a pure white guinea pig
(bb), all the offspring in the first generation (F₁) are black (Bb) because the dominant black gene masks the white one. When
these F₁ guinea pigs (Bb × Bb) are crossed, the second generation (F₂) shows both black and white guinea pigs in the ratio of
3 black : 1 white. This result is similar to Mendel’s pea plant experiment, proving that the laws of inheritance discovered by
Mendel Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation, and Law of Independent Assortment are universal and apply to both plants
and animals.

Ans:- phenotypic ratio of this generation is 3:1 and genotypic ratio of this generation is 2:1. iii) Among them, which plant is purely round-seeded? Why?
r Rr rr
Ans:- The purely round-seeded plant is RR because RR is homozygous dominant, so it will always produce gametes carrying
R and therefore always give round-seeded offspring when self-pollinated.
iv) Which law of Mendel is followed in this result? How?
Ans:- This result follows Mendel’s Law of Segregation. The two alleles (R and r) of a parent separate into different gametes
during gamete formation when F₁ individuals (Rr) self-pollinate, the alleles recombine to give the 1:2:1 genotypic and 3:1
phenotypic ratios seen in F₂. (The Law of Dominance also explains why Rr shows the round phenotype.)
